page: Amazon Web Services c8id.metal-96xl is a bare-metal compute-optimized server driven by an Intel x86_64 architecture. The hardware configuration provides 192 physical cores and 384 dedicated virtual cores operating at a base frequency of 3.9 GHz, paired with 768 GB of system memory. Because it functions as a bare-metal deployment, applications gain direct access to the underlying hardware resources without hypervisor-induced latency or resource contention.

Integrated directly into the instance is 22800 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, offering high local input and output performance for data-intensive processing without dependence on remote block volumes. Interconnect performance is governed by a 100 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, accommodating extensive multi-node communication, rapid file staging, and data movement across parallel processing topologies.

The hardware profile emphasizes extreme compute density and fast temporary storage, maintaining a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio. This balance restricts the server from memory-heavy analytics caches, representing an explicit tradeoff favoring raw instruction throughput over memory per core. As a result, the server delivers high resource efficiency for compute-heavy workloads such as distributed batch processing, high-performance computing, media transcoding, and large data transformation pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services c8id.metal-96xl is a bare-metal compute-optimized instance built on x86_64 Intel processors. The server features 192 physical cores and 384 dedicated virtual cores operating at a 3.9 GHz clock frequency, coupled with 768 GB of system RAM to deliver a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory profile. Direct bare-metal access eliminates hypervisor overhead, ensuring consistent execution across parallelized operations. For storage and communication throughput, the platform bundles 22800 GB of direct-attached NVMe SSD instance storage and delivers a 100 Gbps baseline network capacity. The architecture trades higher per-core RAM capacity for core density and rapid local disk access, making it less aligned with memory-bound workloads. Instead, c8id.metal-96xl provides strong operational efficiency for distributed computing, intensive data transformation, large-scale batch analysis, CI/CD compilation farms, and high-performance engineering simulations demanding massive multi-core execution and local I/O performance.
